motivation: The permanent is a central object in algebraic complexity, and lower bounds for arithmetic circuits are notoriously hard, especially when division gates are allowed.
method: Refines the critical-locus method using a column-deletion recurrence, maximal-rank theorem for inclusion matrices, circuit-dependent formal deformation through valid division, finite flatness, and a norm argument.
result: Establishes the stated n^2 log log N lower bound over characteristic zero for permanent circuits with valid division.
conclusion: This advances classical algebraic circuit complexity but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Global Framework For Dynamics And Criticality Of Bound States In The Continuum
authors: Keren Wang, Lujun Huang, Wei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) exhibit rich momentum-space dynamics, including merging, annihilation, and reconnection across symmetry directions and bands. Yet these phenomena have largely been explained case by case, without a unified framework to classify or predict them. Here we develop a global symmetry-equivariant theory for the dynamics of nondegenerate and degenerate BICs. We show that BIC dynamics can be classified into [MATH]-, [MATH]-, and [MATH]-processes according to root motion, which not only encompass the reported dynamics in [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] systems but also include previously unrecognized ones. More importantly, we reveal that distinct dynamics are bridged by the criticality of BICs through a , in which selected direction--band branches acquire higher-order radiation zeros. Such a theory predicts which branches become critical and how to tune system parameters to realize them. Following this framework, we construct high-order BICs in full-wave calculations, realizing [MATH] nondegenerate criticality and [MATH] single-branch and band-paired degenerate criticalities. Our framework provides a systematic route to understanding, discovering, and selectively controlling BIC dynamics and high-[MATH] states.
tldr: A symmetry-equivariant global framework classifies and predicts the momentum-space dynamics and criticality of bound states in the continuum (BICs) in photonic and wave systems.
motivation: BIC dynamics such as merging, annihilation, and reconnection have previously been explained only case by case, with no unified theory to classify or predict them across symmetry directions and bands.
method: The authors develop a global symmetry-equivariant theory of nondegenerate and degenerate BICs, classifying their root motion into distinct process types and identifying criticality points where direction-band branches acquire higher-order radiation zeros.
result: The theory reproduces known BIC dynamics in C2, C4, and C6 systems, predicts new dynamics, and guides full-wave constructions of high-order BICs including nondegenerate criticality and single-branch and band-paired degenerate criticalities.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic route to understanding, discovering, and selectively controlling BIC dynamics and high-order states, but it lies in photonics/wave physics rather than any of the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-system directions.

title: Breakdown Of Axis Separability And Structured Inversion In Finite-Domain Normalized Position Measurements: A Quadrant Photodetector Case Study
authors: Zhiqian Su
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-domain normalized spatial measurements combine an incident field, geometric support, local response, and channel weighting. These operations can break an otherwise separable response, so accurate single-axis calibration alone does not establish separability of a multidimensional measurement. We represent normalized readouts as channel-weight expectations under a parameter-dependent effective measure. For fixed reception and channel operators, local sensitivity is the covariance between the channel weight and the source score. This representation distinguishes axis separability, parameter mixing, and local recoverability, and applies at the appropriate detector level to continuous-electrode position-sensitive detectors, Shack--Hartmann and pyramid wavefront sensors, back-focal-plane split detection, and finite pixel arrays. A quadrant photodetector (QPD) provides an analytically tractable case. Starting from the complete two-dimensional power integrals, we identify the spatial-moment origin of its lowest-order cross term. Axis calibration and system symmetry then constrain the inverse map, giving Axis-Anchored Cross-Residual Inversion (ACRI). Numerical tests of this QPD realization support the sensitivity relations and show that the constrained cross correction substantially reduces the off-axis bias retained by single-axis inversion. The results illustrate how the general measurement representation guides inverse construction, with performance bounded by the working domain, calibration state, and preserved symmetries.
tldr: The paper analyzes axis separability and constructs a structured inversion method for finite-domain normalized position measurements, using quadrant photodetectors as a case study.
motivation: Accurate single-axis calibration does not guarantee separability in multidimensional spatial measurements, so a better understanding of cross-axis coupling and inversion is needed for position-sensitive detectors.
method: The authors represent normalized readouts as channel-weight expectations under a parameter-dependent effective measure, derive local sensitivity via covariance, and constrain the inverse map using axis calibration and system symmetry to obtain Axis-Anchored Cross-Residual Inversion (ACRI).
result: Numerical tests on a quadrant photodetector confirm the sensitivity relations and show that the constrained cross correction substantially reduces off-axis bias compared to single-axis inversion.
conclusion: The general measurement representation and ACRI framework provide a systematic way to guide inverse construction for finite-domain position measurements, with performance limited by the working domain, calibration state, and preserved symmetries.

title: Multidimensional Dynamical Centrality From Green Functions In Complex Networks
authors: Hao Yu Yusen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional centrality measures provide compact descriptions of node importance, but they emphasize specific structural relations and do not directly resolve the temporal and spectral organization of dynamical perturbation responses. Building on the Green function of a linearized networked system, we develop a multidimensional framework for dynamical node characterization. From the same response function, we extract three complementary indicators---Influence, Efficiency, and Distortion---that quantify cumulative response strength, temporal rate of response, and spectral concentration, respectively, together with a contribution matrix that resolves these quantities into source--target pathways. As a numerical demonstration, we apply the framework to weighted Kuramoto--Sakaguchi dynamics on heterogeneous Barab\'asi--Albert networks. The three indicators distinguish implanted dynamical node classes through complementary dimensions of the perturbation response, while remaining strongly coupled to conventional topological centralities. These results demonstrate how a common dynamical response can be decomposed into distinct, physically interpretable characteristics rather than represented by a single aggregate descriptor. We finally discuss the scope and limitations of the linear-response assumption and extensions to time-dependent and nonlinear regimes.
tldr: A multidimensional dynamical centrality framework derived from the Green function of a linearized networked system, applied to Kuramoto-Sakaguchi dynamics on Barabási-Albert networks.
motivation: Conventional centrality measures emphasize static structural relations and fail to resolve the temporal and spectral organization of dynamical perturbation responses in complex networks.
method: Starting from the Green function of a linearized networked dynamical system, the authors extract three complementary indicators—Influence, Efficiency, and Distortion—plus a source-target contribution matrix, and test these on weighted Kuramoto-Sakaguchi dynamics over heterogeneous Barabási-Albert networks.
result: The three indicators separate implanted dynamical node classes along complementary dimensions while remaining strongly coupled to conventional topological centralities.
conclusion: A single dynamical response can be decomposed into distinct, physically interpretable characteristics rather than a single aggregate descriptor, though the linear-response assumption limits validity beyond weak perturbations.

title: Observation Of Symmetry Breaking In Time-varying Scattering Systems
authors: Miguel Verde, David Globosits, Thomas F. Allard, Calvin M. Hooper, Simon A. R. Horsley, Stefan Rotter, Paloma A. Huidobro, Ian R. Hooper
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From the Higgs mechanism to magnetic ordering, spontaneous symmetry breaking organizes physics across scales. Whether an analogous transition governs waves scattered by periodically driven structures has remained an open experimental challenge. Here we demonstrate a universal symmetry-breaking transition in a periodically driven finite scattering system. By measuring the multispectral Floquet scattering matrix of a strongly modulated microwave resonator, we observe a transition from an unbroken symmetry regime with scattering eigenvalues of equal modulus to a broken symmetry regime where their moduli split apart, through an exceptional point. At parametric resonance, this transition culminates in coherent perfect absorption, where a tailored multispectral input state is completely absorbed without outgoing radiation, the singular limit of the underlying transition. Because it arises from the general algebraic structure of the Floquet scattering matrix rather than from implementation-specific details, this transition should occur broadly in such systems. Unlike instability phenomena in bulk driven media, it emerges in the eigenstructure of a finite scattering operator that couples waves across multiple frequency channels. Our results establish Floquet scattering as an experimentally accessible platform for the observation of symmetry breaking and for dynamic wave control in driven photonic systems.
tldr: The paper experimentally observes a symmetry-breaking transition in the Floquet scattering matrix of a periodically driven microwave resonator, culminating in coherent perfect absorption.
motivation: It remains an open experimental challenge whether an analogue of spontaneous symmetry breaking can govern waves scattered by periodically driven structures.
method: The authors measure the multispectral Floquet scattering matrix of a strongly modulated microwave resonator and analyze its eigenvalue structure.
result: They observe a transition from an unbroken regime with equal-modulus scattering eigenvalues to a broken regime with split moduli, passing through an exceptional point and leading to coherent perfect absorption at parametric resonance.
conclusion: The findings establish Floquet scattering as an experimentally accessible platform for observing symmetry breaking and for dynamic wave control in driven photonic systems.

title: Null Controllability Of A Stochastic Parabolic Equation With A Space-Dependent Analytic Noise Coefficient
authors: Yu Wang Qi L\"u
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a stochastic parabolic equation on the [MATH]-dimensional flat torus [MATH], [MATH], whose only control acts in the drift. The multiplicative-noise coefficient is adapted and may depend jointly on the sample point, time, and space. Its spatial profiles are assumed to be real analytic with a uniform positive radius of analyticity, while the corresponding analytic norm is only required to be square integrable in time, uniformly along sample paths. We prove a state-only observability inequality with an [MATH]-in-time mean-square observation norm and deduce null controllability from every measurable spatial set of positive measure by one adapted drift control. The same one-time interpolation estimate also yields approximate controllability to arbitrary square-integrable random terminal targets. The proof is based on a direct analytic energy estimate for the adjoint state, followed by propagation of smallness and a telescoping argument.
tldr: The paper establishes null and approximate controllability for a stochastic parabolic PDE on a flat torus with a space-time-sample-dependent analytic multiplicative noise coefficient.
motivation: Controllability of stochastic parabolic equations is a fundamental question in stochastic control theory, particularly when the noise coefficient is irregular in time but has analytic spatial structure.
method: The authors prove a state-only observability inequality via a direct analytic energy estimate for the adjoint state, combined with propagation of smallness and a telescoping argument.
result: They obtain a mean-square-in-time observability inequality and deducing null controllability from any measurable set of positive measure using a single adapted drift control, as well as approximate controllability to arbitrary square-integrable random targets.
conclusion: The work extends controllability results for stochastic parabolic equations to settings with jointly adapted, space-analytic noise coefficients, relying on propagation-of-smallness techniques rather than classical Carleman estimates.

title: Tessellated Isotropic Elastic Lattice Spring Model For Quasi-Brittle Fracture
authors: Meng-Cheng HE D. M. LI
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasi-brittle fracture is prevalent in concrete, rock, ceramics, composites, and masonry, and its simulation faces a trade-off among accuracy, efficiency, and simplicity. The classical Lattice Spring Model (LSM) captures cracking via bond breakage without remeshing, but its elements are empirical and limited to a few tessellable shapes with fixed Poisson's ratios. We propose a tessellated Isotropic Elastic Lattice Spring Model (IELSM) that discretizes continua into polygonal elements with axial springs and a volumetric constraint, achieving isotropic elasticity on arbitrary polygonal tessellations. Macroscopic isotropy reduces to governing equations whose solvability gives a theoretical criterion for element admissibility, proving conventional tessellable elements and extending to arbitrary regular N-gons and concave elements. Exploiting boundary interpolation compatibility with finite elements, IELSM is assembled by direct node sharing, without interface elements or kinematic constraints. Coupled with an isotropic damage model, a pure bending test and four fracture benchmarks show that the coupling preserves displacement accuracy, yields crack paths and load-displacement curves agreeing with experiments and outperforming standard FEM, and is insensitive to mesh refinement. IELSM can also be restricted to damage-prone regions, with the remainder modeled by finite elements via node sharing. For the benchmarks, this reduces nodes by 41.2-80.9% and CPU time by 34.2-85.2% versus full-domain IELSM. The framework advances IELSM element construction from empirical trial and error to theoretical determination and simplifies coupling to node sharing, offering a balanced route for complex quasi-brittle fracture analysis.
tldr: The paper introduces a tessellated Isotropic Elastic Lattice Spring Model (IELSM) that discretizes continua into polygonal elements with axial springs and a volumetric constraint to simulate quasi-brittle fracture with isotropic elasticity on arbitrary polygonal meshes.
motivation: Classical Lattice Spring Models capture cracking via bond breakage without remeshing but rely on empirical element constructions limited to a few tessellable shapes with fixed Poisson's ratios, creating a trade-off among accuracy, efficiency, and simplicity.
method: IELSM combines axial springs with a volumetric constraint on arbitrary polygonal tessellations, deriving governing equations whose solvability yields a theoretical admissibility criterion, and couples this with an isotropic damage model while exploiting finite-element boundary interpolation compatibility for direct node sharing.
result: Benchmarks including a pure bending test and four fracture cases show preserved displacement accuracy, crack paths and load-displacement curves matching experiments and outperforming standard FEM, with mesh-refinement insensitivity; restricting IELSM to damage-prone regions reduces nodes by 41.2-80.9% and CPU time by 34.2-85.2%.
conclusion: The framework moves IELSM element construction from empirical trial-and-error to theoretical determination and simplifies coupling to node sharing, offering a balanced approach to complex quasi-brittle fracture analysis.

title: Conditional Preservation Of Chimera States Under Equitable Network Coarse-graining
authors: Margherita Bert\`e, Thierry Njougouo, Paolo Sarti, Tommaso Gili
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chimera states, characterized by the coexistence of coherent and incoherent dynamics in networks of coupled oscillators, are among the most intriguing collective phenomena in nonlinear systems and are strongly shaped by the underlying topology and initial conditions. Their analysis in large-scale networks remains computationally demanding and motivates the development of coarse-graining strategies that reduce network size while retaining the essential dynamical features of chimera behavior. In this Letter, we investigate whether equitable-partition-based quotient graphs can preserve chimera patterns under substantial reductions of network size. Using nonlocally coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) oscillators, we exploit the fact that, for an equitable partition, the full-network dynamics restricted to the associated cluster-synchronous subspace coincide exactly with the quotient dynamics. We ask whether this structural exactness is sufficient to preserve chimera signatures after the network size reduction. Our results show that this is not necessarily the case: agreement between quotient and full-network chimera dynamics depends on the equitable partition, and exact quotient dynamics do not necessarily guarantee the transverse stability of the corresponding full-network trajectory. Importantly, when the cluster-synchronous solution becomes transversely unstable, the full network may depart from the exact quotient trajectory while remaining in a macroscopic chimera regime. Therefore, structural exactness and dynamical preservation are distinct requirements, and transverse stability provides a complementary criterion for assessing quotient-based coarse-graining of chimera states.
tldr: This paper studies whether equitable partition quotient graphs preserve chimera states in networks of nonlocally coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators, showing that structural exactness does not guarantee dynamical preservation.
motivation: Chimera states in large networks are computationally expensive to analyze, motivating coarse-graining methods that reduce network size while retaining essential dynamics.
method: The authors use equitable-partition-based quotient graphs and examine the cluster-synchronous subspace, comparing quotient dynamics to full-network dynamics for nonlocally coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators.
result: They find that exact quotient dynamics do not necessarily imply transverse stability of the corresponding full-network trajectory, and the full network can depart from the exact quotient trajectory while still exhibiting macroscopic chimera behavior.
conclusion: Structural exactness and dynamical preservation are distinct requirements, and transverse stability provides a complementary criterion for quotient-based coarse-graining of chimera states.

title: Topology Of Bound States In The Continuum From The Angular Structure Of Leading Radiation
authors: Ya Yan Lu Nan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the angular structure of the leading radiation associated with a bound state in the continuum (BIC) directly encodes topology, identifies the critical conditions for topological-charge transitions, and reveals the bifurcation of new BIC families under structural variations. For at-[MATH] BICs, rotational and time-reversal symmetries determine the allowed angular harmonics of the leading radiation and hence the possible topological charges. As an example, we directly identify a BIC with [MATH] in a [MATH] dielectric slab with a triangular lattice of circular air holes, without computing nearby resonances or tracking the merging of BICs. This BIC is also a super-BIC, exhibiting an ultrahigh quality factor [MATH] along all directions in momentum space, where [MATH] is the wavevector detuning parameter. We also use a [MATH] structure to analyze a topological transition and the associated bifurcation of off-[MATH] BICs. Our results may find applications in resonant, structured, and topological photonics.
tldr: The angular structure of leading radiation from bound states in the continuum directly encodes topological charges and reveals topological transitions and bifurcations in photonic structures.
motivation: Topological properties of bound states in the continuum (BICs) are usually inferred by tracking nearby resonances or monitoring BIC merging, which can be cumbersome. The authors aim to extract topology more directly from radiation patterns.
method: They analyze the angular harmonics of leading radiation allowed by rotational and time-reversal symmetries for at-Γ BICs, and use a C6v structure to study topological transitions and off-Γ BIC bifurcations.
result: They identify a BIC with topological charge 2 in a triangular-lattice dielectric slab without computing nearby resonances, and show it is a super-BIC with ultrahigh quality factor scaling as 1/k^6 along all directions.
conclusion: The work links radiation angular structure to BIC topology and may find applications in resonant, structured, and topological photonics.

title: Sensing Assisted Satellite Backhaul With Fbl Ul And Broadcast Dl For Massive IoT
authors: Tijana Devaja, Milica Petkovic, Israel Leyva-Mayorga, Dejan Vukobratovic, Cedomir Stefanovic
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Massive Internet of Things (IoT) networks operate with short packets whose reliability is limited by finite block- length (FBL) effects, while remote deployments increasingly rely on Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites for backhaul connectivity that is sensitive to atmospheric attenuation. In this paper, we pro- pose a unified end-to-end framework for satellite-assisted massive IoT networks that jointly models uplink FBL random access, sensing assisted satellite backhaul, and worst user broadcast downlink transmission. Uplink reliability is characterized using stochastic geometry, while atmospheric sensing and conservative SNR margins enable FBL-safe backhaul adaptation. Numerical results reveal an optimal uplink access probability due to the tradeoff between spatial reuse and FBL reliability, and show that sensing assisted backhaul margins significantly improve robustness against attenuation uncertainty.
tldr: The paper proposes an end-to-end framework for massive IoT networks using LEO satellite backhaul with finite blocklength uplink and broadcast downlink, assisted by atmospheric sensing.
motivation: Massive IoT deployments in remote areas rely on satellite backhaul, but short-packet finite blocklength effects and atmospheric attenuation limit reliability.
method: The framework jointly models uplink random access using stochastic geometry, sensing-assisted satellite backhaul with conservative SNR margins, and worst-user broadcast downlink.
result: Numerical results identify an optimal uplink access probability balancing spatial reuse and FBL reliability, and show that sensing-assisted backhaul margins improve robustness against attenuation uncertainty.
conclusion: The integrated design enhances reliability for massive IoT over satellite links, but the work is purely classical communication and not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Fast-Slow Mean-Field Forward-Backward Stochastic Systems
authors: Yihao Sheng, Fuke Wu, George Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an averaging principle for a class of multiscale mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations and identify several novel phenomena that are absent from classical fast-slow systems. In contrast with classical fast-slow systems, the effective dynamics cannot in general be obtained by simply freezing deterministic slow parameters and averaging against the invariant measure of the resulting fast equation. The appropriate averaging object is instead provided by a frozen fast dynamics in a random environment and its associated conditional invariant measures, which retain the coupling between the slow state and its distribution. The forward-backward structure creates a further obstruction: local averaging estimates need not remain stable when propagated over an arbitrary time horizon. We identify a uniform restart stability condition for the averaged system under which this obstruction can be overcome. Using a joint lifted semigroup for the state-law dynamics, together with a two-scale discretization and a Gordin-type decomposition, we prove strong averaging for both the forward and backward components with optimal convergence rate [MATH]. As an application, we apply the general theory to a class of mean-field stochastic control problems and develop an efficient algorithm for solving such mean-field control problems.
tldr: The paper establishes an averaging principle for multiscale mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations and applies it to mean-field stochastic control.
motivation: Classical fast-slow averaging principles fail for mean-field forward-backward systems because the effective dynamics involve conditional invariant measures and suffer from propagation instability over long horizons.
method: The authors use a joint lifted semigroup for state-law dynamics, two-scale discretization, and a Gordin-type decomposition to prove strong averaging for both forward and backward components.
result: They obtain strong averaging with an optimal convergence rate under a uniform restart stability condition and develop an efficient algorithm for mean-field control problems.
conclusion: The work extends averaging theory to a novel class of mean-field forward-backward systems and provides a computational tool for stochastic control, but it is purely classical stochastic analysis.

title: Functional Dynamic Mode Decomposition: Learning Infinite-dimensional Systems From Data
authors: Eirini Ioannou Stefan Klus
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) is a data-driven method that computes the best linear approximation of the underlying dynamical system and decomposes the dynamics into a superposition of characteristic spatiotemporal patterns. Originally introduced by the fluid dynamics community, DMD and its extensions have found widespread use in many other research areas such as molecular dynamics, climate science, engineering, finance, and neuroscience. Applications include dimensionality reduction, forecasting, system identification, control, and spectral clustering. In order to apply DMD to partial differential equations, the spatial domain is typically first discretized using finite difference or finite element techniques, thus implicitly rendering the problem finite-dimensional. We extend projected and exact DMD to infinite-dimensional systems. Rather than estimating matrices from vector-valued observations, our DMD variants learn finite-rank operators from functional data such as observables, densities, or wavefunctions. We show that conventional DMD algorithms can be regarded as special cases of their functional DMD counterparts. All results will be illustrated with the aid of guiding examples. We focus in particular on Koopman, Perron-Frobenius, and Koopman-von Neumann operators associated with graphons, ordinary differential equations, and stochastic differential equations.
tldr: This paper extends dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to infinite-dimensional systems by learning finite-rank operators from functional data.
motivation: DMD is widely used for data-driven modeling but is typically applied after spatial discretization, which forces a finite-dimensional approximation. The authors aim to handle infinite-dimensional systems directly using functional data such as observables, densities, or wavefunctions.
method: The authors develop functional projected and exact DMD variants that learn finite-rank Koopman, Perron-Frobenius, and Koopman-von Neumann operators from functional data rather than vector-valued observations, showing standard DMD as special cases.
result: The proposed functional DMD methods are illustrated on guiding examples involving graphons, ordinary differential equations, and stochastic differential equations.
conclusion: Functional DMD provides a principled way to learn infinite-dimensional dynamical systems from data, generalizing conventional DMD and enabling operator approximation without explicit spatial discretization.

title: Agent Approval Laundering: Transitive Effects Beyond The Approved Invocation
authors: Jinqian Zhang (institute Of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy Of Sciences, School Of Cyber Security, University Of Chinese Academy Of Sciences), Haojun Xia (institute Of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy Of Sciences, School Of Cyber Security, University Of Chinese Academy Of Sciences), Shujiang Wu (beihang University), Jingkun Yue (state Key Laboratory Of Networking And Switching Technology, Beijing University Of Posts And Telecommunications), Xia Zhang (institute Of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy Of Sciences, School Of Cyber Security, University Of Chinese Academy Of Sciences), Zhangpei Cheng (institute Of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy Of Sciences, School Of Cyber Security, University Of Chinese Academy Of Sciences), Bibo Tu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding-agent approval interfaces bind a human decision to a command or tool call, while developer tools execute the transitive workflow that invocation activates. Package installation can run lifecycle hooks and write files; an MCP call can exercise network authority. We call the resulting record-coverage failure approval laundering: the durable record names the entry invocation but omits effects exercised by its workflow. We present the first systematic security analysis of this record-to-closure relation in agent systems. We formalize closure-bound approval over six effect classes and derive an information limit: identical policy-visible fields can require different effect-specific decisions, so no record-only policy can guarantee both. The Approval-to-Action Security Benchmark binds approval objects and decision-time metadata to post-execution evidence. Across 111 fixed approval-object/trace pairs, residual records fall from 40 under explicit fields to 17 with command semantics and 13 with decision-time metadata. Across 11 fixed-SHA executions, the ladder reaches zero metadata residuals; two exact mappings recur across three product frontends. For prospective recovery, effect-bound records commit frozen, source-backed predictions and provenance before authorization. On 17 prespecified holdout workflows, predictions achieve 0.926 macro recall and 0.941 macro precision; binding them cuts residual effects from 10 to 3. A Claude Code PreToolUse integration carries the frozen record through the permission path without automatic approval. These results establish approval laundering as a measurable, recurrent record-coverage failure despite truthful invocation identity. They motivate binding each invocation before authorization to a source-backed prediction of its workflow's transitive effect boundary and preserving that binding with the decision.
tldr: The paper identifies and formalizes 'approval laundering,' a record-coverage failure in coding-agent approval interfaces where durable records omit transitive effects exercised by approved invocations, and proposes effect-bound records to improve prospective recovery.
motivation: Approval interfaces bind human decisions to commands or tool calls, but developer tools execute transitive workflows whose effects (e.g., lifecycle hooks, network access) can exceed what the approval record captures.
method: The authors formalize closure-bound approval over six effect classes, derive an information limit for record-only policies, introduce the Approval-to-Action Security Benchmark with 111 approval-object/trace pairs and 11 fixed-SHA executions, and evaluate effect-bound records with predictions and provenance.
result: Residual records decrease from 40 to 13 using decision-time metadata, and on 17 holdout workflows effect-bound predictions achieve 0.926 macro recall and 0.941 macro precision, cutting residual effects from 10 to 3.
conclusion: Approval laundering is a measurable, recurrent record-coverage failure despite truthful invocation identity, motivating binding each invocation before authorization to a source-backed prediction of its transitive effect boundary.

title: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, And Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion
authors: Qi Pang, Virginia Smith, Wenting Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings such as finance, healthcare, and software engineering, where agents coordinate through natural-language messages. The same channels, however, let colluding agents exfiltrate confidential information or coordinate unauthorized actions, and steganography can hide such communication inside outputs that look ordinary to an auditor reading the transcript. Existing provably undetectable LLM steganography protocols are not suited to realistic deployments. High-capacity schemes assume a symmetric setting where the receiver can reproduce the sender's output distribution, the state-of-the-art protocol for asymmetric agents has very low capacity, and most approaches rely on a pre-shared secret key. We make the threat of undetectable agent collusion concrete with Codetta, a high-capacity steganographic protocol for independently deployed agents in realistic asymmetric settings. Codetta combines a shared public model that estimates the communication channel, a sampling mechanism that preserves the sender's output distribution, and an adaptive error-correcting code. It further removes the pre-shared key through a steganographic key exchange that lets independently deployed agents establish a shared key while keeping the transcript computationally indistinguishable from ordinary model outputs. Across three agent workloads and three sender models, Codetta achieves up to [MATH] the capacity of the state-of-the-art asymmetric protocol, and its key exchange establishes a shared key with about 80k visible tokens at an empirically certified failure probability of at most [MATH]. These results show that effectively undetectable collusion is becoming feasible between independently deployed agents, so auditing must go beyond inspecting communication transcripts.
tldr: Codetta is a high-capacity, keyless, provably undetectable steganographic protocol enabling colluding LLM agents to communicate covertly in asymmetric deployment settings.
motivation: Multi-agent LLM systems coordinate via natural-language messages, and steganography lets colluding agents exfiltrate data or coordinate unauthorized actions while remaining invisible to transcript auditors. Existing undetectable steganography schemes are impractical: high-capacity ones assume symmetric receivers, the asymmetric state-of-the-art has low capacity, and most require a pre-shared secret key.
method: Codetta couples a shared public model that estimates the communication channel, a sampling mechanism that preserves the sender's output distribution, and an adaptive error-correcting code; it also introduces a steganographic key exchange that lets independently deployed agents agree on a key while the transcript stays computationally indistinguishable from ordinary model outputs.
result: Across three agent workloads and three sender models, Codetta attains up to an order-of-magnitude capacity gain over the state-of-the-art asymmetric protocol, and its key exchange establishes a shared key using roughly 80k visible tokens at an empirically certified failure probability.
conclusion: Effectively undetectable collusion between independently deployed LLM agents is becoming feasible, implying that auditing of multi-agent systems must extend beyond inspecting communication transcripts.

title: Tp-criv: A Framework For Third-Party Challenge-Response Identity Verification Of Ai Models
authors: Teruki Sano, Minoru Kuribayashi, Masao Sakai, Shuji Isobe, Eisuke Koizumi, Zhang Zhang, Satoru Matsumoto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models are increasingly deployed through remote services, making model misappropriation a growing concern. Existing approaches, including watermarking, fingerprinting, and model similarity analysis, primarily rely on predefined evidence or direct behavioral comparison and do not explicitly evaluate whether the claimant currently possesses and can utilize model-dependent information relevant to the claimed model identity. In this paper, we propose Third-Party Challenge-Response Identity Verification (TP-CRIV) for AI models. TP-CRIV targets a third-party verification setting in which the verifier has neither white-box nor API access to the claimant's model, can interact with the suspicious deployed service only through its ordinary black-box inference interface, and does not require protocol-specific cooperation from the service provider. Under these constraints, the framework enables the verifier to obtain empirical evidence as to whether the claimant locally possesses a model satisfying a predeclared identity relative to the deployed model. Verification is conducted under fresh, previously undisclosed requirements and network isolation, so that the demonstrated capability cannot rely on online external assistance after challenge disclosure. The resulting evidence is interpreted relative to independently specified and calibrated matching and non-matching operating situations and is statistical rather than cryptographic. We instantiate TP-CRIV for CNN image classifiers using probability-control-based witness generation. Experiments on ten ImageNet-pretrained TorchVision models demonstrate clear same/cross-model separation and finite-challenge verification using independently calibrated thresholds.
tldr: A framework for third-party identity verification of AI models using challenge-response under black-box access.
motivation: AI models are increasingly deployed via remote services, raising concerns about model misappropriation, and existing methods do not evaluate whether a claimant possesses model-dependent information.
method: TP-CRIV uses probability-control-based witness generation with fresh, undisclosed challenges and network isolation, requiring only black-box interaction with the deployed service.
result: Experiments on ten ImageNet-pretrained models show clear same/cross-model separation and finite-challenge verification using calibrated thresholds.
conclusion: TP-CRIV provides statistical evidence for model identity verification without protocol-specific cooperation, potentially aiding in detecting model misappropriation.

title: A Measure-Theoretic Derivation Of Zadeh Fuzzy Logic
authors: Angshul Majumdar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zadeh fuzzy logic is normally introduced by assigning scalar membership degrees and postulating standard complement, minimum conjunction, and maximum disjunction. We derive this calculus from a strictly positive atomless normalized Boolean measure algebra. Equality of measure sends Boolean complement uniquely to [MATH], but it cannot send meet to a single-valued operation: the exact scalar image of conjunction is the overlap interval [MATH]. We quantify the information lost under scalarization, prove that no nontrivial measure-preserving compression can retain meet, and show that the overlap operation is associative as a hyperoperation. Zadeh conjunction [MATH] is then forced as the unique nondecreasing idempotent selection and is realized globally by nested event chains; its De Morgan dual is Zadeh disjunction [MATH]. Thus the min--max--standard-negation calculus follows from measure theory once the nesting commitment is made explicit. The \Luk{} and product conjunctions arise as minimum-overlap and independent-factor selections, clarifying alternative scalarizations. Exact minimax results, an ordered-valued extension, and a three-dimensional realization obstruction delimit what scalar fuzzy logic retains from Boolean structure.
tldr: The paper derives Zadeh fuzzy logic from a measure-theoretic Boolean algebra, showing that min–max–standard-negation calculus arises once a nesting commitment is made explicit.
motivation: Zadeh fuzzy logic is usually introduced axiomatically by postulating membership degrees and operations, so the author seeks a foundational derivation from measure theory.
method: The author starts with a strictly positive atomless normalized Boolean measure algebra and analyzes measure-preserving scalarizations of Boolean complement, meet, and join, using overlap intervals and hyperoperations.
result: Boolean complement maps uniquely to standard negation, but conjunction cannot be sent to a single-valued operation without losing meet; Zadeh conjunction is forced as the unique nondecreasing idempotent selection, and disjunction follows by De Morgan duality.
conclusion: The min–max–standard-negation calculus follows from measure theory under an explicit nesting commitment, while Łukasiewicz and product conjunctions arise as alternative scalarizations; exact minimax results and a three-dimensional obstruction delimit scalar fuzzy logic.

title: Counterexamples To A Conjecture Of Kamenetsky On Oeis A173419
authors: Rosario Patan\`e
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Define a(n) as the number corresponding to the shortest computation using only addition, subtraction, or multiplication, as A173419 states on the related OEIS page. In a comment to the sequence, D. Kamenetsky conjectured that a(p) [MATH] a(p -1) for every prime. We show that the conjecture is false through four counterexamples below 5000 that satisfy the condition a(p) < a(p -1). They are exactly 3359, 3623, 4909, and 4943.
tldr: The paper disproves a conjecture by Kamenetsky about the OEIS sequence A173419 by exhibiting four prime counterexamples below 5000 where a(p) < a(p-1).
motivation: Kamenetsky conjectured that for the integer-complexity-style sequence A173419 (shortest computation using addition, subtraction, or multiplication), every prime p satisfies a(p) ≥ a(p-1); the author seeks to test and refute this conjecture.
method: Exhaustive computational search of the sequence values for primes below 5000 to identify primes violating the conjectured inequality a(p) ≥ a(p-1).
result: Four counterexamples were found: 3359, 3623, 4909, and 4943, all satisfying a(p) < a(p-1), and they are claimed to be exactly the ones below 5000.
conclusion: The conjecture is false, as demonstrated by these explicit counterexamples in pure integer-complexity arithmetic.

title: Repulsive Mean-Field Couplings And Self-Consistent Transfer Operators
authors: Roberto Castorrini, Stefano Galatolo, Matteo Tanzi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a one-dimensional self-consistent transfer operator generated by a repulsive mean-field coupling. The interaction admits a natural interpretation as a myopic relocation dynamics balancing congestion and uniformly distributed resources. Using the quantile representation of probability measures, combined with self-consistent transfer operators methods, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a physically relevant invariant measure for the system and characterize it explicitly through a nonlinear fixed-point equation. We then show that the corresponding finite-particle equilibrium converges to the continuum equilibrium with optimal order in Wasserstein distance and establish a quantitative thermodynamic limit.
tldr: The paper studies a one-dimensional self-consistent transfer operator with repulsive mean-field coupling and proves existence, uniqueness, and convergence to a continuum equilibrium with optimal Wasserstein rate.
motivation: The interaction is motivated as a myopic relocation dynamics balancing congestion against uniformly distributed resources, and the authors aim to characterize its invariant measure and finite-size convergence.
method: They use the quantile representation of probability measures combined with self-consistent transfer operator techniques to derive a nonlinear fixed-point equation for the invariant measure.
result: They establish existence and uniqueness of a physically relevant invariant measure, explicitly characterize it via a nonlinear fixed-point equation, and show finite-particle equilibrium converges to the continuum equilibrium with optimal order in Wasserstein distance, giving a quantitative thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous mathematical foundations for mean-field dynamics with repulsive coupling, but it lies outside the quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Proper Scoring Rules For Survival Times
authors: Philip Dawid
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note presents a general form for a proper scoring rule that can be used for possibly right-censored survival data without requiring any knowledge or assumptions about the censoring process.
tldr: This note derives a general proper scoring rule for evaluating probabilistic forecasts of possibly right-censored survival times without assuming any model for the censoring mechanism.
motivation: Proper scoring rules are central to assessing probabilistic predictions, but survival data are often subject to right-censoring whose process may be unknown or difficult to model.
method: The paper characterizes a general form of proper scoring rule that remains valid for right-censored survival data without requiring knowledge or assumptions about the censoring distribution.
result: A broad class of proper scoring rules for survival times is presented, extending standard scoring-rule theory to the censored-data setting in a censoring-agnostic way.
conclusion: The proposed scoring rules enable principled evaluation of survival predictions when the censoring process is unspecified, with potential use in statistical forecasting and model comparison.

title: Reflective Projective Billiards In The Plane: Odd Periods, Period Five, And Metric Rigidity
authors: Jorge Lucas Gonz\'alez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study polygonal projective billiards whose reflection law is constant on each side. We give a single explicit family with an open set of periodic trajectories for every period at least three, including every odd period, and identify the previously known centrally projective examples as a special parameter value. For period five we describe the full scalar-monodromy variety, prove its irreducibility, and show that every configuration preserves a nonzero quadratic form. Under the stated distinct-centre and non-collinearity hypotheses that form is nondegenerate; this yields an explicit unirational classification of the convex five-reflective locus. We also relate the definite members to spherical billiards and prove that, among analytic simply connected constant-curvature surfaces with geodesic walls, only the sphere can carry an open family of periodic trajectories. For general complete analytic ambients with global wall reflections we prove compactness and a common period for the geodesic flow. The arguments reduce the billiard return map to products of harmonic homologies and separate the algebraic closure condition from the strict first-impact inequalities.
tldr: The paper classifies polygonal projective billiards with constant reflection law on each side, giving explicit families of periodic trajectories and proving metric rigidity results for constant-curvature surfaces.
motivation: Projective billiards generalize classical billiard dynamics by allowing a projective reflection law, and questions about existence of periodic orbits and their algebraic structure are central to integrable and algebraic dynamics.
method: The authors reduce the billiard return map to products of harmonic homologies, analyze the period-five scalar-monodromy variety, prove its irreducibility, and separate the algebraic closure condition from strict first-impact inequalities.
result: They construct one explicit family with open sets of periodic trajectories for every period at least three (including all odd periods), fully describe the period-five locus with a preserved nondegenerate quadratic form, obtain a unirational classification of the convex five-reflective locus, and show that only the sphere admits such open families among analytic simply connected constant-curvature surfaces.
conclusion: The work links projective billiards to spherical billiards and yields compactness and common-period results for geodesic flows with global wall reflections, providing new algebraic and rigidity insights in geometric dynamics.

title: Intrinsic Hilbert Metrics On Cones Of Equivalent Norms
authors: Juan Rafael Acosta-Portilla
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a Banach space and let [MATH] denote the family of equivalent norms on [MATH]. We study Hilbert projective metrics on its projectivization [MATH] induced by ambient cones of nonnegative functions, with particular attention to the intrinsic Hilbert metric induced by the cone [MATH]. First, we show that the symmetric logarithmic metric on [MATH] is the Hilbert projective metric induced by the cone of nonnegative real-valued functions, and we characterize the ambient cones that induce the same metric. We then study the intrinsic order on [MATH]. For this purpose, we introduce the triangular defect [MATH] and prove that two norms [MATH] belong to the same intrinsic part if and only if their triangular defects are uniformly comparable, that is, [MATH] for some [MATH]. This yields an explicit formula for the intrinsic Hilbert metric in terms of the pointwise comparison of the norms and of their triangular defects. tldr: The paper studies Hilbert projective metrics on the projectivization of the space of equivalent norms on a Banach space, characterizing the intrinsic Hilbert metric via triangular defects.
motivation: Hilbert projective metrics on cones arise in various mathematical contexts, and the paper aims to understand their structure on spaces of equivalent norms through ambient cones of nonnegative functions.
method: The author introduces the triangular defect for norms and uses it to characterize when two norms belong to the same intrinsic part, deriving an explicit formula for the intrinsic Hilbert metric.
result: It is shown that the symmetric logarithmic metric is the Hilbert projective metric induced by the cone of nonnegative real-valued functions, and that the intrinsic Hilbert metric can be expressed via pointwise comparison of norms and their triangular defects.
conclusion: The map from the intrinsic cone order into a canonical product cone preserves the Hilbert metric on each intrinsic part, providing a concrete representation of the intrinsic order.

title: Null Controllability On Measurable Sets For The Complex Cubic Ginzburg--Landau Equation
authors: Can Zhang Yu Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the null controllability of the complex cubic Ginzburg--Landau equation with controls supported on general space-time measurable sets. Starting from a positive-measure control set, we use a slicing argument to obtain time slices of uniformly positive spatial measure. This yields uniform spectral inequalities on the slices, which are the key ingredient in constructing quantitative stabilizing feedbacks. A density-point argument provides a sequence of shrinking intervals accumulating at the density point, on which the active times have a uniform positive density. We then apply a time-iteration scheme with piecewise feedback laws and increasing decay rates. Iterating the resulting stabilization estimates shows that the closed-loop solution reaches the zero state at the selected density point. This provides a constructive approach to the local null controllability on measurable control sets for nonlinear parabolic equations.
tldr: The paper proves local null controllability for the complex cubic Ginzburg-Landau equation with controls supported on general space-time measurable sets.
motivation: The work aims to extend controllability results for nonlinear parabolic PDEs to irregular control sets of positive but possibly small measure.
method: It combines a slicing argument to obtain spatial slices of uniform positive measure, uniform spectral inequalities, a density-point argument, and a time-iteration scheme with piecewise feedback laws.
result: The closed-loop solution is shown to reach the zero state at a selected density point, yielding a constructive approach to local null controllability on measurable control sets.
conclusion: This provides a new constructive controllability result for the complex cubic Ginzburg-Landau equation, though it falls outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: On Degeneration Of Tetrahedra Under Longest-edge N-section Refinement
authors: Sergey Korotov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.29153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every integer [MATH], we construct explicit tetrahedral counterexamples showing that repeated longest-edge (LE) n-section refinement does not, in general, preserve shape regularity, contrary to long-standing conjectural expectations. For [MATH], the construction disproves the finite-family conjecture put forward by Adler in 1983 and the non-degeneracy conjecture for tetrahedral longest-edge bisection formulated by Rivara and Levin in 1992. It also shows that the sharper higher-dimensional diameter decay suggested by Stynes in 1983,following his 1980 planar finite-similarity result, cannot hold for arbitrary tetrahedra. For [MATH], it disproves the published non-degeneracy conjecture for tetrahedral longest-edge trisection formulated in 2011 by Su\'arez, Abell\'on, Abad and Plaza on the basis of numerical experiments. The resulting infinite descendant sequences violate both the minimum and maximum angle conditions. For [MATH], the selected edge is always the unique longest edge at every refinement step. The two-step recurrence used in the construction exhibits two distinct degeneration behaviors: a flat-tetrahedron regime for [MATH] and a skinny-tetrahedron regime for [MATH]. The degenerating sequences can also be realized within conforming partitions generated by the conforming LE n-section algorithm. For both the classical and the conforming LE n-section algorithms, the maximal element diameter tends to zero as the number of refinement steps tends to infinity, regardless of which longest edge is chosen. Thus diameter convergence, and even conformity, do not prevent shape degeneration. These algorithms should therefore be used with care in applications requiring uniform shape regularity.
tldr: The paper constructs explicit tetrahedral counterexamples showing that repeated longest-edge n-section refinement can degenerate in shape despite diameter convergence, disproving several long-standing non-degeneracy conjectures.
motivation: Longest-edge refinement is widely used in mesh generation and finite element methods, where shape regularity is often assumed to guarantee good numerical behavior.
method: The author builds explicit tetrahedral counterexamples using a two-step recurrence, analyzing longest-edge n-section refinement for n=2,3,4 and both classical and conforming algorithms.
result: The constructions disprove conjectures by Adler, Rivara and Levin, Suárez et al., and show that both minimum and maximum angle conditions can be violated while element diameters still tend to zero.
conclusion: Diameter convergence and conformity do not prevent shape degeneration, so longest-edge n-section refinement should be used with care in applications requiring uniform shape regularity.

title: An Exposition Of Gpt Astra's Proof Of Lower Bound On Dp Continual Counting
authors: Jalaj Upadhyay
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this note is to give a detailed proof, to the best of our understanding, of the recent presentation by Harrison and Leeman (arXiv:2609.17650v01 and arXiv:2609.17650v02) of the proof by Astra on the lower bound for differentially private continual counting. We believe a more natural and easy proof is possible and hope that this note will help in that effort. Prior to the initial preprint by Harrison and Leeman (arXiv:2609.17650v01), Bairaktari and Larsen (arXiv:2607.00876) gave an elegant proof to show a lower bound of [MATH] for both pure and approximate-DP continual counting, and in personal communication had informed us that they have a proof of optimal [MATH] for pure-differential private continual counting as well. They have subsequently published their [MATH] bound, which is now a joint work of Bairaktari, Dahl, and Larsen (arXiv:2607.00876v3). Their new result is an elegant extension of their technique for approximate-differential privacy. Although the two proofs are technically different, the Astra argument uses related tree geometry introduced in Bairaktari and Larsen.
tldr: This note provides an exposition of GPT Astra's proof of a lower bound on differentially private continual counting.
motivation: The paper aims to clarify and present a more natural and accessible proof of a recent lower bound result for differentially private continual counting, following works by Harrison and Leeman and by Astra.
method: The author gives a detailed, expository proof of Astra's lower bound argument, drawing connections to tree geometry used in Bairaktari and Larsen's earlier techniques.
result: The note reconstructs and explains the lower bound proof for pure and approximate differential privacy in continual counting, highlighting the relationship between different proof approaches.
conclusion: The exposition seeks to aid understanding and potentially stimulate a simpler proof of the optimal lower bound for differentially private continual counting.

title: zkSAS: Practical Zero-Knowledge Proofs For Verifiable Spectrum Access Management
authors: Nishat F. Purbasha, Ifteher Alom, Eric W. Burger, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou, Yang Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic Spectrum Access (DSA) through the Spectrum Access Systems (SAS) elevates spectral efficiency, yet existing centralized models face allocation logic opaqueness and a lack of independent verifiability. While blockchain-based SAS architectures offer transparency and verifiability by default, they introduce critical privacy risks and prohibitive on-chain computational overhead. We introduce zkSAS, a practical zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) system designed to address the verifiability and privacy gaps in SAS deployments, with direct applicability to both the existing CBRS SAS model and blockchain-based SAS models. The system features a suite of ZKP circuits, encompassing proofs of allocation constraint validity and proofs of move list validity to verify that channel assignments and move list-based incumbent protection measures, respectively, adhere to regulatory constraints without exposing sensitive user data. Comprehensive evaluation of our prototype in both centralized and blockchain-based settings indicates that while proof generation scales with spectrum user population, verification remains lightweight and constant-time. We envision that zkSAS offers a scalable and practical path to secure, verifiable dynamic spectrum sharing.
tldr: zkSAS is a zero-knowledge proof system for verifiable and privacy-preserving dynamic spectrum access management in both centralized and blockchain-based SAS deployments.
motivation: Existing centralized spectrum access systems lack transparency and independent verifiability, while blockchain-based alternatives introduce privacy risks and high on-chain computational overhead.
method: The authors design a suite of ZKP circuits that prove allocation constraint validity and move list validity without exposing sensitive user data, and evaluate a prototype in centralized and blockchain settings.
result: Proof generation scales with the number of spectrum users, but verification remains lightweight and constant-time in both settings.
conclusion: zkSAS provides a scalable and practical path to secure, verifiable dynamic spectrum sharing, though it is a classical cryptography and networking contribution.

title: Exponential Correlation Bounds For Polynomials
authors: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Pooya Hatami, Chin Ho Lee, Shachar Lovett, Avishay Tal, Emanuele Viola
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the XOR of [MATH] majorities on disjoint blocks of \(\ell\) bits has correlation at most \((2d/)^k\) with every degree-\(d\) polynomial over \(\mathbb F_2\). By known techniques, this implies pseudorandom generators with polylogarithmic seed length for low-degree polynomials over [MATH] and for alternating circuits with parity gates.
tldr: Proves exponential correlation bounds for the XOR of majorities against low-degree polynomials over F2, yielding pseudorandom generators for low-degree polynomials and parity-alternating circuits.
motivation: Correlation bounds and pseudorandomness for low-degree polynomials are central problems in classical computational complexity theory.
method: Analyzes the correlation of XORs of majorities on disjoint blocks with degree-d polynomials over F2, using Fourier-analytic and probabilistic techniques.
result: The XOR of majorities has correlation at most (2d/ℓ)^k with any degree-d polynomial over F2, which implies PRGs with polylogarithmic seed length for low-degree polynomials and alternating circuits with parity gates.
conclusion: The paper advances classical complexity theory and pseudorandomness but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Blockchain-Enabled Artificial Intelligence And Ai Agents For Secure Data Sharing And Cybersecurity Applications
authors: Harsh Verma
abstract: ArXiv:2609.28843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchain and artificial intelligence (AI) are converging into a single infrastructural layer for securing data sharing, model integrity, and autonomous decision-making across distributed systems. This paper presents a meta-synthesis that draws together four constituent studies covering adversarial machine learning, AI-powered anomaly detection in cloud environments, automated vulnerability patching by multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines, and the broader landscape of securing AI systems across their lifecycle and situates their findings within the emerging literature on blockchain-enabled AI and autonomous AI agents. Each constituent study addresses a distinct point of failure in modern AI-driven security operations: the integrity of training data and model behavior, the reliability of real-time monitoring, and the trustworthiness of automated code remediation. We argue that blockchain's properties of immutability, decentralized consensus, and verifiable provenance directly address a gap common to all three: the difficulty of establishing trust in data, models, and autonomous agents that operate without a central authority. Building on real-world research on blockchain-secured data sharing, federated learning, and multi-agent coordination, we propose a layered reference architecture that couples adversarially hardened models, blockchain-anchored data provenance, AI-driven anomaly detection, and smart-contract-governed multi-agent remediation. We conclude by identifying open problems in scalability, privacy-transparency trade-offs, and the governance of autonomous agents that must be resolved before such integrated systems can be trusted in production-critical environments.
tldr: A meta-synthesis proposing a layered reference architecture that combines blockchain provenance, adversarially hardened AI models, anomaly detection, and smart-contract-governed multi-agent LLM remediation for secure data sharing and cybersecurity.
motivation: Modern AI-driven security operations lack a way to establish trust in training data, models, and autonomous agents operating without a central authority, motivating a decentralized trust layer.
method: Meta-synthesis of four constituent studies (adversarial ML, AI anomaly detection in cloud, multi-agent LLM vulnerability patching, lifecycle AI security) situated within blockchain-enabled AI literature, yielding a proposed layered architecture.
result: The paper argues blockchain's immutability, decentralized consensus, and verifiable provenance address trust gaps common to data, model, and agent integrity, and outlines an integrated architecture coupling these components.
conclusion: Integrated blockchain-AI-agent systems require further work on scalability, privacy-transparency trade-offs, and autonomous-agent governance before production-critical deployment.

title: NP-Hardness Of Bounded Distance Decoding For Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Jun Zhang Daqing Wan
